$comment: VR-only image enrichment, keyed by BARE FILE NAME. Same contract as projects.json: enrichment, never content. The flat site's alt attribute is still the primary label and is used whenever there is no entry here — this file exists because an alt is written for a screen reader reading a page in order ('Sebastian Esteva — candid photo 1' is fine there, since the surrounding page says what the carousel is) while a photo-cloud tile floats alone in a dome with nothing around it to supply the context. CAPTIONS ARE FIRST PERSON — 'a night I ran', never 'a night he ran'. Sebastian's call, 2026-09-09: the site speaks as him, and a caption that slips into the third person reads as a museum label about someone else. `caption` replaces the alt for the cloud; `exclude` drops the image from the cloud entirely; `project` is an href override for the handful of files whose name does not start with their project's stem, which is how the catalog normally infers it. Nothing here changes the flat site.

contact-photo-framed-for-mosaic.jpg.$why: The same photograph as contact-photo-professional.jpg, cropped and registered to line up with the mosaic underneath it. It exists only as the top layer of the flat site's hero dissolve, and its alt describes the COMPOSITE ('with a digital mosaic and VR headset illustration overlaid on one eye'), which is a caption for an effect the cloud does not run. In the cloud it showed up as a second, identical portrait carrying a description of something not in the picture.
